stage_name: S4 slice 4/N continuation: Home Assistant discovery migration + HA-discovery tombstone (plan required changes #14 HA portion, #16-#19)
note_on_commits: No new commit created; commits are only made on explicit user request. This work is uncommitted and directly continues S4-mqtt-v1-cutover (implementation-evidence/S4-mqtt-v1-cutover-completion.json), all uncommitted on top of 8d09cfa (merge of PR #45).
sequencing_note: User's explicit correction after the cutover pass's summary flagged HA discovery migration as urgent-but-deferred: 'проет ще не в продакшн тож зміни можливі радикальні без додаткових міграцій' (the project isn't in production yet, so radical changes are possible without additional migrations). This pass therefore completes the HA-discovery portion of plan #14 together with the #16-#19 migration itself, in the same window, exactly as the plan's own cutover-order section (Stage S4, steps 4-5) already specified.

components/mqtt_bridge/mqtt_discovery.cpp (rewritten in place -- no parallel legacy/v1 discovery code kept, unlike the topic/serializer files, since the caution that justified that pattern no longer applies: all 5 entity builders now derive unique_id/object_id/device-identifiers from gateway_id_hex+device_id_hex, point state/command/availability topics at the v1 tree, and gained an availability_template needed by the v1 availability payload's JSON format; new build_legacy_discovery_tombstone helper + build_legacy_homeassistant_discovery_tombstones public function)

components/mqtt_bridge/mqtt_bridge.cpp (publish_homeassistant_discovery rewritten: new one-time legacy-discovery-tombstone sweep via legacy_discovery_tombstoned_, gateway_id_hex_ threaded into the new-discovery call, schema-change cache lookup switched from short_addr-keyed find_cached_device_by_short to device_id_hex-keyed find_cached_device_by_device_id_hex -- the now-unused find_cached_device_by_short was removed; devices with no resolved device_id_hex are skipped; reset_sync_cache() resets the new tombstone-sweep flag)

docs/architecture/MQTT_API_V1.md (title/Section 1 updated to cover items 10-19 across three passes; Section 3.5 simplified; new Section 3.7 documents the discovery migration and tombstone; Section 4 deduplicated/renumbered; Section 5 cppcheck note corrected)

frozen_decisions_applied: S4 MQTT required change #16: unique_id, the discovery topic's object_id segment, and the device 'identifiers' field are all now derived from both DeviceId (device_id_hex) and the canonical FD-17 GatewayId (gateway_id_hex) -- zgw_<gateway_id_hex>_<device_id_hex>[_<suffix>] -- so cloning the firmware image to different hardware yields a different discovered identity while reboot/reset on the same hardware does not.

S4 MQTT required change #17: build_legacy_homeassistant_discovery_tombstones() publishes deletion (empty retained) payloads for the old short-address discovery entities, and MqttBridge::publish_homeassistant_discovery() runs that sweep before its new-discovery-publish loop in the same function call, matching the plan's literal ordering.

S4 MQTT required change #18: entity type/capabilities are preserved across the identity change by construction -- the same 5 entity builders (switch/power, sensor/temperature, binary_sensor/occupancy, binary_sensor/contact, sensor/battery) with the same capability-gating logic (has_temperature, occupancy_state != kUnknown, etc.) were kept, only their identifiers/topics changed. The 'exactly one controlled deletion-and-recreation migration' language is satisfied by the tombstone sweep firing exactly once per MqttBridge lifetime (legacy_discovery_tombstoned_).

S4 MQTT required change #19: every entity's command_topic (switch/power) now targets the v1 DeviceId-keyed power/set topic; state_topic/availability_topic were also moved to the v1 tree in the same change (not explicitly named by #19's text, but required for the discovered entity to remain functional given Section 3.4 of this document already moved all live-content publishing to v1-only).
The HA-discovery portion of plan #14 (deferred by the prior cutover pass) is now implemented, per the user's explicit confirmation that no production deployment exists to protect.

discovery_identity_rewrite.detail: mqtt_discovery.cpp rewritten in place (not paralleled) to derive every identifier from gateway_id_hex+device_id_hex and every topic reference from the v1 tree. A new availability_template field was added to every entity, a necessary correctness consequence of the v1 availability payload being JSON rather than the legacy bare online/offline string. build_homeassistant_discovery_messages() now requires a non-empty device.device_id_hex and a non-null gateway_id_hex, skipping devices without a resolved identity.

legacy_discovery_tombstone.detail: build_legacy_homeassistant_discovery_tombstones() builds all 5 possible legacy discovery topic tombstones unconditionally for a given short_addr (a caller cannot generally know which subset a device actually had published). Wired into publish_homeassistant_discovery() via a new one-time-per-bridge-lifetime trigger (legacy_discovery_tombstoned_), separate from the state/telemetry/availability tombstone sweep in sync_snapshot() because discovery publishing bypasses the pending-publication queue entirely (direct hal_mqtt_publish() calls).

remap_safety_for_discovery.detail: publish_homeassistant_discovery()'s schema-change cache lookup switched from short_addr-keyed to device_id_hex-keyed (find_cached_device_by_device_id_hex, new), mirroring the outbound-publishing remap-safety fix from the prior cutover pass -- a short_addr remap no longer looks like a new device to the discovery-republish decision either, avoiding a spurious (harmless but wasteful) discovery republish. The now-unused short_addr-keyed find_cached_device_by_short was removed rather than left as dead code.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: state_topic and availability_topic in the discovery payloads were moved to the v1 tree, even though plan #19's text only names 'discovery command templates' (i.e. command_topic) explicitly.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Leaving state_topic/availability_topic pointed at the legacy tree while Section 3.4 of this document already moved all live-content publishing to v1-only exclusively would mean every discovered entity silently stops updating the moment this firmware runs -- the entity would exist in HA but never report a new value. This is a correctness requirement implied by the rest of this pass's own prior work, not a new scope decision.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: None negative -- discovered entities remain functional. This is recorded because it is technically broader than the plan's literal #19 text, not because it caused any regression.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: No parallel 'legacy discovery' code path was kept in mqtt_discovery.cpp the way mqtt_topics.hpp/mqtt_serializer.hpp were kept alongside their v1 counterparts in the earlier passes.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The earlier passes' pattern (keep legacy code reachable for host tests/dev use, just unregistered/unsubscribed in production) existed specifically to avoid an irreversible production behavior change without review. Discovery-building is a pure function with no production-reachability distinction to preserve (nothing ever called the legacy discovery builders directly except the one call site inside publish_homeassistant_discovery(), which this pass rewrote outright) -- keeping a second, now-completely-unused copy of 5 near-identical builder functions would be dead weight with no test or dev-profile value.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: None -- legacy discovery topic strings needed only for tombstoning are reconstructed by the small, dedicated build_legacy_discovery_tombstone() helper, which is a much smaller surface than keeping full duplicate entity builders.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The MQTT command-result topic's payload contract remains undesigned, unchanged from the prior two passes.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Unchanged reasoning: blocked on the same OperationResultStore domain-unification blocking the HTTP operations-poll route.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: No consumer of this topic exists yet in either direction; purely additive once built.
